nodes.body: **Bug: cluster bars block hover on the abnormal dots they are meant to preserve.** Clusters render *after* `dots.map(...)` (line 436), and `.clusterBar` has no `pointer-events: none`, so the full-height rect (x from `cx-3` to `cx+3`, plotTop→baseline) sits on top of the abnormal dots (circles at `cx ± 3.5`) and swallows their `onMouseEnter` except for a ~0.5px sliver. The whole point of "abnormal statuses … never absorbed into a counted cluster" is that they stay individually hoverable — in any tall column they are not. Fix: `pointer-events: none` on `.clusterBar` (moving the `<title>` elsewhere), or render clusters before dots.

The cap guide only steps when `retune.value` is a number, but `adaptive_connections` retunes can carry `true` / `"10-80"` / `{min, max}` values. `capFromRetune` in `ConnectionsView.tsx` handles exactly this via `adaptiveMaxFromValue`, so the same retune steps the cap guide on the Usage → Connections lens but not on the Timeline band. Same issue for `capValues` at lines 285–286 (band y-scale). Suggest exporting `capFromRetune` from `connectionHistory.ts` and reusing it here.

Nit (non-blocking): `popoverCloseTimer` is never cleared on unmount, so a pending 250ms close fires `setPopover` after the component is gone (harmless no-op in React 18, but a `useEffect(() => () => clearTimeout(...), [])` cleanup is cheap).

**Bug: `poolRetunes` drops `change.cleared`, misrepresenting cleared overrides.** A cleared change carries `value: null` (cf. `effectiveConfig.ts`: "Cleared restores the launch value — distinct from setting null"), so downstream surfaces render it as a literal transition: the Connection Log row and the ◆ tooltip show `max_connections 20 → null` (reads as "limit removed") when the pool actually reverted to its launch cap, and `capFromRetune` / the Timeline cap guide keep the stale 20 instead of restoring the launch value. `ConfigChangedChip` handles this case correctly ("override cleared → launch value"); `PoolRetune` should carry `cleared` (and ideally the resolved restored value) so the usage surfaces can too.

`PoolRetune` now carries `cleared`; log rows and ◆ tooltips render "override cleared → launch value", and `capFromRetune` (now shared from `connectionHistory.ts`) takes a `launchCap` argument so cap guides step back to the lane's launch cap on cleared. Lanes don't carry per-knob launch values, so the guide restores `configuredMax` (the value the guide starts from) rather than resolving each knob individually.

This comparator violates the sort contract for equal-time same-kind pairs: two config rows at the same timestamp return `-1` for both `(a,b)` and `(b,a)` (two controller rows return `+1`/`+1`). That is a real case — one `ConfigUpdate` touching two knobs yields two retunes with the identical provenance timestamp — and their relative order becomes engine-defined rather than update order. Fix: `a.time - b.time || (a.kind === b.kind ? 0 : a.kind === "config" ? -1 : 1)`.

`String(retune.previous)` / `String(retune.value)` render `[object Object]` for structured values — e.g. a mid-run `adaptive_connections = {min: 2, max: 50}` retune. Same in the ◆ tooltip in `ConnectionsView.tsx` (line 290). This PR already adds `formatConfigValue` in `config/ConfigChangedChip.tsx`, which JSON-stringifies structures — reuse it here.

Nit: the chip labeled "Events" filters to the **config retune** rows, while the actual runtime events (controller scale changes, rate limits) live under "Controller" — a user clicking "Events" to find rate limits gets config changes. "Config" would be the accurate label (and `eventCount` is really a retune count).

**Dead code: `ModelCard` has no call sites anywhere in the repo** (it was already unreferenced on main — nothing imports it, so nothing supplies the new `configUpdates` prop). The ~80 lines of new changed-affordance logic here never render. Either wire the component back up or do not extend it — as-is this will drift silently.

Resolved by reverting the extension: `ModelCard.tsx` is back to its main state (it was already unreferenced on main, so extending it only added unreachable code). If it gets wired back up later, the changed-value affordance should come from a shared entries-builder helper alongside `ConfigValueCell` rather than a second copy of the ConfigCard algorithm.

Duplication: this entries-builder (wrap changed knobs in `{_html: <ConfigValueCell/>}`, then append rows for changed knobs missing from the effective config) is the same ~35-line algorithm as `configEntries` in `ModelCard.tsx`, differing only in which fold/changes pair feeds it. Worth extracting a shared helper next to `ConfigValueCell` in `@tsmono/inspect-components/config`.

With the dead `ModelCard` extension reverted (see the ModelCard thread), this entries-builder now exists only here, so there is no duplication left to extract. If a second consumer appears, extracting a helper next to `ConfigValueCell` is the right move.

The `scores` category is unreachable: `rowCategory` only ever returns `config` / `tags` / `runtime` (no `HistoryRow` kind maps to `scores`), so this chip is permanently rendered as a disabled "Scores (0)". If score-edit rows are planned, a TODO would clarify; otherwise drop the category from `HistoryCategory`, the chip list, and the defaults in `TimelineTab.tsx`.

Nit: this is not per-log — `propertyBags` live in the app slice keyed only by bag name (the `usage-connections` bag referenced here is the same), so band toggles leak across logs in a session: hide "Active samples" on log A and it is hidden on log B too, and the `useShowTimelineForModel` deep-link toggle sticks for every log sharing that model name. The PR description also claims "Band-picker state persists per log". Either scope the key by log path or fix the comment/description.

Now that `connections_by_row` / `connections_window` / `onShowConnectionLog` are no longer passed here (and the two other `ModelTokenTable` callers never passed them), the entire connection-lane path inside `ModelTokenTable.tsx` and the whole `ConnectionsLane.tsx` component (+ its module.css) are unreachable, and duplicate the new `PoolLane`. Suggest removing them in this PR, since this refactor is what orphaned them.

Doc nit: this docstring says `value` is the "launch value when cleared", but `changesFor` copies `change.value` verbatim (`null` for cleared changes) — it never sees the launch config, so it cannot substitute the launch value. Current consumers all guard on `cleared` first, so it is latent, but a future consumer trusting the docstring would render "none" for a restored knob. Related: `concurrencyChanges` has no test coverage, and no test asserts `value` on a cleared change.

Micro-nit: this reverse role-alias lookup is duplicated in `UsagePanel.tsx` (`logRoles`, lines 145–150) — same `Object.entries(role_aliases).filter(...).map(...)` inversion; could be one small shared helper.

Micro-nit: `running` is assigned in the loop below but never read after the initial `if` — the loop-body assignment is dead, and the variable can be reduced to `data.start === data.peak` in the condition.

**Bug: `fmtCompact` can render `1:60`.** `m` floors the raw seconds but `s = Math.round(seconds % 60)` rounds up to 60 without carrying: `fmtCompact(119.6)` gives `m = 1`, `s = 60`, i.e. `"1:60"` instead of `"2:00"`. Any fractional time in `[x*60+59.5, (x+1)*60)` triggers it, and `working_time`/`total_time` are fractional seconds. Round once up front (`const t = Math.round(seconds)`) and derive `m`/`s` from `t`.

**Bug: post-run retunes leak into the Connections band's y-scale and cap guide.** `poolRetunes` has no post-run concept and this renderer never filters by time, so a post-run retune (a) inflates `dataMax` (line 298), squashing the in-run trace, and (b) gets clamped by `x()` to `plotRight` in the `capSegments` loop (line 321), emitting a zero-width final segment whose `cap N` label renders at the right edge over the real in-run cap -- displaying a cap that was never in effect during the run.

Example: run ends at T, someone amends `generate.max_connections` 50 -> 500 at T+2h. The diamond correctly moves to the post-run gutter, but the band rescales to ~550 and labels "cap 500" at `plotRight`. `guideSegments` already skips `postRun` markers (`timelineData.ts:193`) -- this band should apply the same filter (e.g. drop retunes with `timestamp > runEnd`). The `PoolLane` in `ConnectionsView.tsx` (Usage -> Connections lens) has the same exposure via `capValues`/`yMax` since its window also ends at `completed_at`.

**Bug: `limitCrossReference` doesn't skip post-run markers.** The filter is only `marker.kind !== "config" || marker.time <= completed`, so a *post-run* amendment of e.g. `message_limit` produces the callout "message_limit was changed at <date> -- samples after that ran under a different limit" on every limit-terminated dot -- but no samples ran after that change; the run was already over. Add `|| marker.postRun` to the skip condition (matching `guideSegments`).

**Bug (running logs): still-running samples are synthetically terminated at `window.end`.** Each running sample contributes a `-1` delta at `window.end`, so for a `started` log the ACTIVE SAMPLES trace steps down to 0 at the live edge -- indistinguishable from "everything finished". Correct for cancelled/crashed runs, wrong while the eval is live. Consider skipping the end delta (holding the line flat to the right edge) when the log status is `started`.

Fixed in 65878f8: `activeSamplesSeries` takes a `running` flag (TimelineTab passes `evalStatus === "started"`). On a live eval, samples with no `completed_at` contribute no end delta, so the trace holds flat to the right edge; on finished logs the synthetic step-down at `window.end` is kept — there a missing `completed_at` really does mean cancelled/crashed.

**Bug: the cap-guide loop conflates "not a cap change" with "cap removed".** `capFromRetune` returns `undefined` both when a retune doesn't step the cap *and* when the cap ceases to exist, and `continue` keeps drawing the stale value:
- Launch config has no `adaptive_connections` (`configuredMax` undefined). A retune sets `adaptive_connections: 50` (guide steps to 50); a later retune **clears** the override -> `capFromRetune` returns `launchCap` = `undefined` -> `continue` -> the guide stays at 50 for the rest of the run.
- A retune sets `adaptive_connections: false` (adaptive disabled) -> `adaptiveMaxFromValue(false)` = `undefined` -> guide keeps showing the previous max.

A three-state result from `capFromRetune` (e.g. `number | "none" | undefined`) would let the loop end/suppress the guide. The same loop exists in `TimelineChart.tsx` (~line 324).

**Robustness/security hardening: `in` matches prototype-chain keys, bypassing the unknown-field skip.** `"toString" in knownKeys`, `"constructor" in knownKeys`, and `"__proto__" in knownKeys` are all `true` (inherited from `Object.prototype`), so a crafted or corrupted log with `{"config": "eval", "name": "__proto__", "value": {...}}` passes the guard and `result[change.name] = change.value` swaps the folded object's prototype (log files are untrusted input to the viewer; the pollution is local to the folded object, so severity is low, but the guard's contract is broken). Same pattern at line 105 (`change.name in launchRecord`) and in `changesFor` (line 168). `Object.hasOwn(...)` fixes all three; a test with a prototype-name change would lock it in.

Nit (non-blocking): `connectionWindow`, `buildConnectionLanes` (sorts + aggregates), and `poolRetunes` all recompute on every render -- including mode-toggle and modal open/close renders -- and the fresh `events`/`retunes` identities defeat the `useMemo` inside `ConnectionLogModal`. Wrapping these in `useMemo` keyed on their inputs would fix both.

Nit (non-blocking): when `start === peak !== final` (a pool that only scaled down), this guard skips the peak search so `peakX` stays 0 and the "peak N" label renders at x~4 directly over the "start N" label at x=0. A `start . peak` merge mirroring `peakAndFinalMerge` (or skipping the peak label when it equals start) would fix it.

Nit (non-blocking): a fast swipe across the chip can leave the popover stuck open. `onMouseEnter` sets `isOpen`, but `PopOver` attaches its `mouseleave` listener to `positionEl` in an effect *after* the next render and immediately starts the show timer -- if the pointer already left before the listener existed, the timer still fires and the popover opens with the pointer elsewhere, staying until an outside mousedown. A trigger-side `onMouseLeave` that cancels when the popover hasn't shown yet would harden this.

Nit (non-blocking): if the recorder ever writes a non-integer name under this prefix, `parseInt` yields `NaN` and the comparator returns `NaN`, making the ordering unspecified for *all* entries (and the fold order wrong). Filtering to `Number.isFinite` indices (or a lexicographic fallback) makes the "monotonic integer index" assumption fail safe. Also: `remoteLogFile.test.ts` has a harness for the `start.json` fallback but no coverage for `readJournalConfigUpdates` (numeric ordering, malformed-entry skip, empty case).
Nit (non-blocking): `items: sorted` is never read -- `clusters.map` uses only `cx` and `count`. Dead field.

Nit (non-blocking): `?? []` creates a fresh array identity on every render while summaries are loading, invalidating the `dots`/`window`/`activeSeries`/`rows` memos each time. A stable module-level empty array (the `kNoSummaries` pattern already used in `state/hooks.ts`) avoids the churn.

Nit (non-blocking): this duplicates the private ISO-to-epoch helper in `packages/inspect-components/src/usage/connectionHistory.ts` (touched in this PR), and `poolRetunes` inlines the same parse a third time. One exported helper would cover all three.

**Bug: “View on timeline” from the Connection Log modal leaves the modal open behind the navigation — it reopens unexpectedly the next time the Models tab is shown.** `logModel` lives in a property bag (`useProperty("usage-connections", "log-model")`, line 111), which deliberately survives unmount, and `TabPanel` unmounts unselected tabs. This handler navigates without clearing it, so: open the Connection Log → click “View on timeline” → later click back to the Models tab → the modal pops open again over the tab. Fix: clear before navigating — `(event) => { setLogModel(null); onViewTimeline(logLane.model, event); }`.

**Bug (very large logs): `Math.min(...times)` / `Math.max(...times)` throw `RangeError` once `times` is huge.** `times` gets one entry per terminated sample (line 136), and spreading a large array as arguments hits the JS engine argument-count limit (roughly 65k–125k in V8), so opening the Timeline tab on a very large eval crashes instead of rendering. A running min/max in the existing loops (or a `reduce`) is drop-in safe. Same pattern in `TimelineChart.tsx:230`.

Same spread-over-a-per-sample-array `RangeError` risk as `TimelineTab.tsx:144` — `values` has one entry per `activeSeries` point (up to 2 per sample). `const dataMax = values.reduce((m, v) => Math.max(m, v), Math.max(guideMax, 1))` avoids the argument-count limit.

**Minor bug: cmd/ctrl/shift-click loses the deep-link toggle and mutates the wrong tab.** `setPropertyValue` runs unconditionally before `showTimeline`, but on a modifier-click `showTimeline` opens a *new browser tab*: in the browser build the store isn’t persisted (`resolveStorage()` returns `undefined` outside VS Code), so the new tab never receives the band toggle — while the *current* tab’s timeline gets the Connections band silently switched on even though the user never navigated there. Consider writing the property only on the in-app navigation path (and carrying the toggle in the URL if it should survive into a new tab).

Fixed in 65878f8 by writing the property only on the in-app navigation path — a modifier click no longer flips the current tab's band store. The toggle is not carried in the URL: the new tab falls back to the auto-light default, which turns a model's Connections band on whenever that model was retuned or rate-limited — exactly the models this deep link points at — so the new tab still lands with the band visible in practice.

Nit (reuse): `renderConnections` re-implements `PoolLane`. Lines 295–333 (capValues/dataMax computation, stepped series path builder, cap-guide stepping loop) are a near line-for-line copy of `ConnectionsView.tsx:179–216`. Both already import `capFromRetune` from `connectionHistory.ts`, which is the natural home for shared `buildStepPath` / `capGuideSegments` helpers — and extracting would let the two already-reported issues in this loop (the `continue`-on-`undefined` cap conflation and the post-run-retune leak) be fixed once instead of twice.

Nit: `retuneTransition` (“override cleared → launch value” / `prev → value`) is rebuilt inline in `ConnectionLogModal.tsx:184–189`. This wording already changed once during this PR’s review cycle; a shared helper next to `PoolRetune` in `connectionHistory.ts` keeps the lane tooltip and the log row from drifting.

Nit: third value stringifier. `formatShort` is near-identical to the existing `valueAsString` (`apps/inspect/src/utils/format.ts:30`) and to `formatConfigValue` exported from the new config barrel — all three render the same `ConfigValueChange` data on different surfaces (marker labels vs chip popovers), differing only in the null label. Worth consolidating on one (e.g. `formatConfigValue` with a null-label option).

Consolidated in 65878f8: `formatConfigValue` gained an optional `nullLabel` parameter and `formatShort` is now a one-line delegate (`formatConfigValue(value, "null")`), so the formatting logic exists once. `valueAsString` predates this PR and has its own consumers, so it was left untouched.

Nit (reuse): this button plus its `.timelineLink` CSS re-implement the private `TimelineLink` in `ConfigChangedChip.tsx:41–46`, and the same markup appears again in `ConnectionLogModal.tsx:101–109` and `ConnectionsView.tsx:130`. Exporting `TimelineLink` from the config barrel would delete three copies.

Consolidated in 65878f8: `TimelineLink` is exported from the config barrel (with an optional `className`) and now used here, in the ConfigChangedChip popovers, and in the Connection Log footer — three local copies and their CSS deleted. The fourth site, the ConnectionsView row action, was intentionally left: it's a different affordance (short "Timeline" label styled as a grid action, paired with "Log"), not a restyled copy of this link.

Nit (wrong-not-missing data on partial failure): the per-entry catch swallows a failed *middle* journal read and keeps folding the later updates. Because the fold is last-wins in order, splicing around a gap can make every effective-config surface (Config card, title bars, `continue_on_fail` gating) display a confidently wrong value with no indication. Since tail truncation is safe for last-wins, consider stopping at the first failed index instead of skipping past it (or surfacing the partial-read state).
Nit: `sampleTokens(sample)` is computed twice per popover render (guard at line 738, display here), iterating `model_usage` twice. Hoisting to a local removes the duplicate work and the `!`.

Nit (test coverage): `connectionHistory.test.ts` covers `connectionWindow` / `buildConnectionLanes` / `adaptiveMaxFromConfig`, but the newly exported `poolRetunes` (concurrency-vs-generate routing to `mainModel`, sort, bad-timestamp filtering) and `capFromRetune` (cleared → `launchCap`, adaptive value parsing) have none — exactly the logic this review cycle already found bugs in.

**Post-run retunes still render as in-lane ◆ markers, pinned to the right edge.** This loop maps every entry of `retunes`, and `x()` clamps a post-run timestamp to `timeWindow.end`, so a cap amended after the eval completes draws a violet ◆ and guide line at the right edge of the plot — indistinguishable from a retune that happened at run end. That is inconsistent with the rest of this PR: `capGuideSegments`/`laneCapValues` deliberately window-filter post-run retunes ("post-run amendments never step the guide"), and the Timeline tab renders post-run markers past an axis break. Filtering on `retune.timestamp <= timeWindow.end` here (or rendering post-run retunes distinctly) would align the Usage lane with the other surfaces. Low severity, but it is the one visible-data inconsistency found this round.

Verified still present at HEAD (d6bc18f) — `(retunes ?? []).map(...)` draws every retune, and `x()` clamps post-run timestamps to `timeWindow.end`. Agreed this is the one surface still inconsistent with the window-filtered cap guide; the fix is a `retune.timestamp <= timeWindow.end` filter at this render site (the same `retunes` array feeds the Connection Log, which should keep post-run rows). Keeping open — queued for the next fix pass.
Fixed in 76612fe — the retune markers now filter on `retune.timestamp <= timeWindow.end` before rendering, so post-run amendments no longer draw in-lane; they remain visible in the Connection Log.

Nit (robustness, non-blocking): this module is explicitly hardened against untrusted log JSON (the Object.hasOwn comment below), but `update.changes` itself is unguarded — a journal entry that parses to an empty object (the `as ConfigUpdate` cast in remoteLogFile.ts performs no validation) throws "update.changes is not iterable" and fails the whole header/summary read instead of degrading gracefully. A `?? []` fallback or an Array.isArray skip here and at lines 169/221 would match the hardening posture.

Confirmed still unguarded at HEAD — `for (const change of update.changes)` here, and the equivalent loops in `changesFor` / `concurrencyChanges`, throw on a journal entry whose `changes` is missing or not an array. An `Array.isArray(update.changes)` skip matches the module's hardening posture. Keeping open — queued for the next fix pass.

Fixed in 76612fe — all three loops (`foldConfig`, `changesFor`, `concurrencyChanges`) skip updates whose `changes` is missing or not an array, with a malformed-entry test covering the fold, the changes map, and the concurrency list.

Two nits (non-blocking):

1. `parseInt` is more permissive than the docstring ("non-integer names are ignored"): `1garbage.json`, `-1.json`, and duplicate-index names (`1.json` plus `01.json`) all parse and get folded — negatives sort first. A strict digits-only match on the suffix would enforce the stated contract. Recorder-written logs are unaffected.

2. Entries are fetched with one awaited range-read each, and `readHeader` re-runs this on every `readLogSummary` poll of a running log (nothing caches), so N retunes cost N serial round-trips per poll. Reads could be issued in parallel — order only matters to the fold, and stop-at-first-failure is still expressible over settled results. Retunes are expected to be few, so perf-nit only.

Declining both halves, with rationale: (1) the `Number.isFinite` filter already makes non-numeric names fail-safe, and the recorder only ever writes plain `<n>.json` — a digits-only match would guard against a writer that does not exist (softening the docstring to 'numeric prefix; non-finite ignored' is the cheaper truth-fix if we touch this again); (2) reads are bounded by retune count (typically a handful per run), and parallelizing them would complicate the stop-at-first-failure truncation contract adopted for middle-read failures. Leaving unresolved for @dragonstyle to close if the rationale holds.

Closing per the rationale above, at @dragonstyle's request: the `Number.isFinite` filter already makes non-numeric names fail-safe (the recorder only writes `<n>.json`), and parallelizing a handful of bounded reads would complicate the stop-at-first-failure truncation contract.

Nit: this comment says abnormal statuses are "never absorbed into a counted cluster", but the overflow branch below absorbs them — `shown` keeps at most kMaxDotRows - 1 abnormal dots, and the rest fold into `count` and render as the cluster bar, which is styled completed-green (`.clusterBar` fill #2f7d4f). With e.g. 10 error terminations in one bin, 5 hidden errors read as completed volume and lose their hover popovers. Worth either fixing the comment or keeping overflow abnormal dots visually distinct.

Addressed by the commits since this review: 9b73e49 raised the collapse cap to 25 rows, 6543a3e moved the absorbed count to hover, and d6bc18f makes the collapsed band wear the **dominant absorbed status** rather than always completed-green — a bin whose absorbed dots are mostly errors now renders error-red, and hovering a collapsed bin opens `BinPopover` with the full per-sample list (including absorbed dots), so nothing loses its popover. The 'never absorbed' comment now holds for up to 24 abnormal dots per bin; beyond that the dominant-status band plus the bin popover carry the information. Resolving as addressed.

Nit: if the user toggles off every band chip while markers exist, `cursor` stays 0 so `axisY` is 6 — marker lines run from y1 = kMarkerTop + 6 upward past y2 = 6, and the diamonds and labels overlap the axis line and its labels in a 34px-tall chart. Reachable state; a minimum marker-rail height (or hiding the chart when `bands.length === 0`) would avoid the garble.

Confirmed still reachable at HEAD — with all band chips off and markers present, `cursor` stays 0, `axisY` is 6, and the marker rail collides with the axis line and labels. Plan: a minimum rail height when `bands.length === 0 && markers.length > 0`. Keeping open — queued for the next fix pass.
Fixed in 76612fe — when every band is toggled off, `axisY` gets a minimum rail height (`kMarkerTop + 24`) so marker lines and diamonds clear the axis line and its labels.

Nit: the comment above says the legend is derived from the visible content, and the tag/metadata item below is correctly conditional — but this "config change" item renders unconditionally, so a log with zero config updates still advertises a diamond that never appears on the chart. Guard with `markers.some((m) => m.kind === "config")`.

Confirmed at HEAD — the 'config change' legend item still renders unconditionally while the tag/metadata item is guarded. Will guard it with `markers.some((m) => m.kind === "config")`. Keeping open — queued for the next fix pass.
Fixed in 76612fe — the 'config change' legend item is now guarded with `markers.some((m) => m.kind === "config")`, matching the tag/metadata item.

Nit: these legend hexes (#2f7d4f, #b04a3c, #d4a72c) duplicate `kStatusColor` in TimelineChart.tsx:48 (and `.clusterBar` in the CSS). Exporting the palette (e.g. from timelineData.ts) and reusing it here would keep the legend from silently desynchronizing from the dots on a future color change.

Confirmed at HEAD — the legend hexes are still hardcoded duplicates of `kStatusColor` (plus `.clusterBar` in the CSS). Will export the palette from `timelineData.ts` and reuse it in the legend. Keeping open — queued for the next fix pass.

Fixed in 76612fe — `kStatusColor` moved to `timelineData.ts` and is imported by both `TimelineChart` and the legend; the hardcoded hexes are gone (the `.clusterBar` CSS duplicate was already removed by the collapse rework).

Nit: the legend labels the cap guide "adaptive max", but `capGuideSegments` also steps it for plain numeric max_connections retunes — retune max_connections 20 → 50 with adaptive off and the violet dashed line is mislabeled. Something like "connection cap" would cover both.

Confirmed at HEAD — the legend still reads 'adaptive max' while `capGuideSegments` also steps the guide for plain numeric `max_connections` retunes. Will relabel to 'connection cap'. Keeping open — queued for the next fix pass.
Fixed in 76612fe — legend relabeled 'connection cap'.

Nit: `peakX` is found by matching `e.new_limit === data.peak`, but `buildConnectionLanes` derives the peak from old_limit too — with a gap in the history (an event whose old_limit is above every new_limit), no event matches, `peakX` stays 0, and "peak N" prints at the left edge over "start N" at a y the step path never visits. Only reachable with inconsistent/gappy history, hence non-blocking.

Declining — as noted this is only reachable with inconsistent/gappy history (an `old_limit` above every `new_limit`), where any label placement is arbitrary; extra code to position a label on data the event stream never realized does not seem worth it. Leaving unresolved for @dragonstyle to close if the rationale holds.
Closing per the rationale above, at @dragonstyle's request: only reachable with inconsistent/gappy event history, where any label placement is arbitrary.

Nit (latent): this popover id is deterministic per knob, so two chips for the same knob mounted at once would produce duplicate DOM ids — and the fast-swipe guard at line 94 (document.getElementById) would see the other chip's open portal and skip cancelling, reintroducing the stuck-popover bug it was added to fix. Fine today (ConfigValueCell renders once per knob), but a useId() suffix would future-proof it.

Declining for now — `ConfigValueCell` renders one chip per knob, so duplicate ids are unreachable today, and the deterministic id is what lets the fast-swipe guard find its own portal. Agreed a `useId()` suffix is the right future-proofing if a second mount site for the same knob ever appears; noting that here for whoever adds one. Leaving unresolved for @dragonstyle to close if the rationale holds.

Closing per the rationale above, at @dragonstyle's request: duplicate ids are unreachable today (one chip per knob), and the deterministic id is what lets the fast-swipe guard find its own portal. A `useId()` suffix is the right move if a second mount site for the same knob ever appears.

Nit (consistency): an explicitly-set-null change renders as "20 → null" here (and at line 298), while the same retune in the Connection Log reads "max_connections 20 → none" via retuneTransition/formatConfigValue. If the literal "null" is deliberate (to distinguish from cleared), consider aligning the Connection Log wording instead — either way the two surfaces currently disagree on the same event.

Confirmed at HEAD — the chip popovers render literal 'null' while `retuneTransition` renders 'none' for the same explicit-set-null event. Will align the two surfaces on a single null label through `formatConfigValue`. Keeping open — queued for the next fix pass.

**bug:** The window never covers sample `started_at`, so on a running log the Active-samples band draws a self-crossing path. Live evals get their header synthesized from `_journal/start.json` (`headerFromLogStart`, remoteLogFile.ts:89), which carries no `stats` — `runStart` is undefined and `window.start` falls to the earliest completion/marker time. Every sample still in flight at that moment has `started_at < window.start`, and `activeSamplesSeries` then emits `[{time: window.start, value: 0}, {time: earlier, value: 1}, …]` — non-monotonic in time (timelineData.ts:135 seeds the first point ahead of the sorted deltas). `renderActive` builds the SVG path in array order with no clipping, so the line starts at the left edge at 0 and doubles back leftward off-plot, and the left edge under-reports the pre-window backlog (`stepValueAt` also assumes sorted points). Symmetric case on a finished log: a never-completed sample whose `started_at` lands after the last covered time gets its synthetic `-1` at `window.end` before its real `+1`. Fix: `cover()` sample `started_at` here, or clamp delta times into the window inside `activeSamplesSeries`.
